title: cross-discipline-reliability-play-portfolio-60d
content:
One-line summary:
A 60-day portfolio of 6 small, parallel experiments to raise service reliability signals, accelerate SLO ownership across product teams, and prove low-friction fracture/recovery patterns for model-serving paths.

Context / why this exists:
- We keep seeing outages and near-misses concentrated on routing + KV cache warm-up during bursty traffic (model-serving).
- Teams ask for clear lightweight SLOs but balk at heavy instrumentation work — need small wins to build trust.
- This portfolio is a cross-discipline playset aimed at delivering measurable uptime and latency improvements with minimum process overhead.

High-level objectives (60d):
1) Establish a minimal SLO surface (availability + p50/95 latency) for three critical serving routes.
2) Ship two fast-fallback policies (model variant + region fallback) with automated runbooks.
3) Improve signal fidelity: get end-to-end request tracing + token-level latency breakdown for 80% of traffic.
4) Reduce long-tail latency (> 3s) incidents by 40% on targeted routes.
5) Document rollback and canary checklist to embed into release flow.

Success criteria (quantitative):
- Three routes have SLO dashboards and owner assigned (owner = team + person).
- Prefix/KV cache hit-rate baseline established; second-week experiment shows >=10% token-cost reduction for warm traffic.
- Post-implementation 60-day rolling: long-tail latency events drop by >=40% for instrumented routes.
- Two fallback policies exercised in a chaos-window with successful automated failover < 20s median.

Portfolio (6 parallel plays) — short descriptions + owners:
1) Route SLO bootstrap (owner: Marco Gutierrez)
   - Deliverable: minimal SLO definitions, thresholds, dashboards for 3 routes (text-gen, chat, embeddings).
   - Scope: define p99 availability, p50/p95 latency buckets, error budget policy.
   - Quick win: reuse existing tracing span names; add route tags at ingress.

2) Cache warming & eviction tuning (owner: Leah Kim)
   - Deliverable: KV cache telemetry (hit/miss, cold-warm transitions), eviction policy experiment (LRU tweaks).
   - Scope: experiment 2 eviction configs in staging; measure token-cost and latency impact.
   - Note: instrument a lightweight 'cache-probe' synthetic runner.

3) Fast-fallback policies (owner: Daniel O'Connor)
   - Deliverable: implement model-variant fallback and region-fallback in policy engine; automated runbook.
   - Scope: integrate with smart routing layer; test with load-injection.

4) Observability plumbing (owner: Rina Sato)
   - Deliverable: token-level latency breakdown and request-level traces in our tracing backend for 3 routes.
   - Scope: small SDK change to emit token timing spans, sampling 10% to limit cost.
   - TODO: confirm cost with observability team before enabling p100 sampling.

5) Canary + rollback checklist (owner: Omar Khalid)
   - Deliverable: a prescriptive canary run and automated rollback action that non-devs can trigger.
   - Scope: create a GitHub action + small dashboard with canary health signals and a one-button rollback link.

6) Runbook & escalation rehearsal (owner: Aisha Patel)
   - Deliverable: one-page runbooks per route + SRE-run rehearsal (tabletop + small chaos window).
   - Scope: capture decision tree: when to failover, when to rollback, who to page, and postmortem triggers.

Timeline (week-by-week overview):
- Week 0 (kickoff): alignment workshop (SRE + product + infra + observability). Owners confirm scope and minimal success criteria.
- Week 1: route SLO defs + observability schema changes (tracing span names, tags). Start cache-probe POC.
- Week 2: dashboards + alert rules wired into pager. Canary scaffold created. Start fallback policy integration.
- Week 3: runbook drafts, begin canary runs in staging, execute eviction config A/B on staging.
- Week 4: rehearse escalation, run small blast tests on fallback (staging). Compute metrics.
- Week 5: production canary for 5% traffic, monitor token-level traces. Iterate config.
- Week 6: full 60-day review window; run scheduled chaos window to validate fallbacks; capture outcomes and next steps.

Meetings / cadence:
- Weekly sync (30min): owners + product/obsv rep. Quick unblock + signals check.
- Bi-weekly stakeholder drop-in (15min): exec summary + ask.
- On-call rehearsal: schedule one 2-hour tabletop during week 4.

Instrumentation checklist (minimal):
- Add route tag to ingress span (required).
- Emit per-token timing span for model invocation (sampling 10%).
- KV cache metrics: hits, misses, evictions, time-to-serve (histogram).
- Synthetic cache-probe job: reports cold-start latency once per minute in staging.
- Canary health events: error-rate, p95 latency, cache-hit-rate.

Risks and mitigations (risk threads):
- Risk: Observability costs spike with token-level spans.
  Mitigation: 10% sampling, review after week 2, budget cap on tracing backend.
- Risk: Fallback produces degraded-quality responses and churns on clients.
  Mitigation: fallbacks only for error/timeout classes, not for quality degradation; add header that indicates fallback used; product to document UX.
- Risk: Owners overloaded; work stalls.
  Mitigation: limit scope to minimal viable telemetry + two fallbacks; escalate resourcing to ENG leads if blocked 3 days.

Dependencies:
- Observability quota approval (cost policy) — need signoff from observability manager before token spans wide rollout.
- Routing policy feature flag readiness in platform (PR #1284).
- Capacity for staging load injection from performance infra team.

Stakeholders / notification list:
- Product: Leah (prod lead), Priya (pm-hosted-api)
- Infra / Platform: Marco + infra oncall
- Observability: Rina + observability eng
- SRE: Aisha + SRE rotation leads
- Customer Success: notify for major fallbacks impacting enterprise clients

Open questions (to resolve in kickoff):
- Which three routes are highest priority (suggestion: text-gen-default, chat-context, embeddings-index)?
- What is the acceptable user-visible quality hit for fallback (quantify per route)?
- Confirm tracing budget and sampling governance — who approves overages?

Postpartum / next steps after 60d:
- Compile a short playbook (1–2 pages) with outcomes + standard library of runbooks + templates for oncall.
- Hand off SLO ownership to product teams with SRE mentorship for the next 90 days.
- If successful, scale the portfolio model to 6 more services for the next quarter.

Quick TODO (notes to self):
- [ ] Book kickoff with product + observability + platform next Tue 10am (invite: all owners).
- [ ] Create JIRA epic and link owners (epic: JIRA-SRE-3421).
- [ ] Confirm sampling cost estimate with Rina by EOW.
- [ ] Draft runbook template and put in /confluence/ops/playbooks by week 2.

Raw experiment measurement plan (example):
- Metric: long-tail latency events (>3s) per 100k requests. Baseline: 210/100k. Goal: <=126/100k (40% reduction).
- Metric: cache-hit-rate for top-100 prefixes. Baseline: 64%. Target: >=70% after warmers.
- Metric: fallback median time to recover traffic < 20s.

Notes: keep experiments small, prioritize observability and clear ownership. Don't try to do full-blown SLO productization in this 60d window — this is about a repeatable template and a few measurable wins.

End.
